newsitem.title: GERMANY: Thyssen happy with portfolio shakeout.
newsitem.headline: Thyssen happy with portfolio shakeout.

text.p: German steel group Thyssen Industrie AG's chief executive, Dieter Vogel, said on Monday that he was happy with the progress being made in a plan to shed some five billion marks ($3.1 billion) worth of businesses.
Vogel told Thyssen's annual results news conference that steps had already been taken to dispose of non-core operations with annual turnover of some 2.8 billion marks.
Thyssen was considering options ranging from sales, cooperation deals and closures for 15 of its business areas, Vogel added.
Thyssen last November set a restructuring plan which foresaw focusing and growing its five core businesses of flat steel, elevator manufacturing, car parts, production systems and materials trading.
Five "potential" core businesses were also identified -- construction technology, real estate, industrial services, logistics and telecommunications.
